text: The Patriots' dominant 20-3 victory over the Steelers at Gillette Stadium in their Week 2 home opener came with a significant price: starting right guard Mike Onwenu suffered a broken right ankle that will likely sideline him going forward, adding to an injury list that marred what was otherwise a defensive showcase. TreVeyon Henderson punched in a touchdown as the Patriots' ground game did much of the heavy lifting, though the offense hasn't yet recaptured the rhythm that fueled last season's Super Bowl run—a fact that underscores just how thoroughly the defense carried the day against Pittsburgh. The win marked a historic milestone as the Patriots became the first of the original AFL teams to reach 600 wins, a testament to the franchise's sustained excellence. While Mike Vrabel's squad clearly has the defensive chops to compete this season, the offensive inconsistency and now the loss of Onwenu's availability suggest there are still adjustments to be made before this team hits its stride.
